verification.note: ShareSheetView.swift:372 DrivePicker calls model.pickDrive. ShareSheetModel.swift:118-129 sets destination and state = .ready (or resolveKind). It never touches queue. pickDriveForQueue (ShareSheetModel.swift:203) has no caller. In ShareSheetView.swift:44-58 the confirmation button is Retry only while the state is .stopped(.driveNotAvailable). After pickDrive the state is .ready, so the button becomes Save. save() (ShareSheetModel.swift:145-158) builds a new queue from all shareItems(), so items already saved would be sent again. The queue's own destination (ShareSendQueue.swift:203 pickDrive) is never changed. This breaks I4: the picked drive does not apply to the items not yet saved, and the saved items are resent.

ShareSendQueue.swift:176 (send) and :186 (retry) both call run(non-saved indices, attempt: .first). Only retryItem at :191 chooses .again for .unknown. A queue-level retry() therefore uses .first for items in the unknown state, so the 409-suffix path applies instead of the original-name check. That conflicts with I6/I7 (a retry never takes a suffix). The sheet's Retry button calls model.retry() for .finishedWithFailures, which is the state with unknown items.

ShareSendQueue.swift:449-453: a .transport error from /complete whose code is in isUnreachable (:549-558, includes notConnectedToInternet, cannotConnectToHost, etc.) returns .stopped(.cannotReach) before pollForFile (:461). run() then marks the item .failed (:245-254) and not .unknown, with the retry offer only. The claim matches the code. Whether this is a defect is a judgement call: I6 stops the queue when the server is unreachable, but also says that after an unanswered /complete the item is saved when by-path finds it. The connection may drop after the server received /complete, and the code does not poll in that case. The offer is .retry, which re-inits with .first instead of the original-name check, so a duplicate with a suffix is possible.

ShareSendQueue.swift:207-220: cancel() only sets cancelling and state = .closing. It calls client.cancelInFlight() only in the chunk, complete and polling phases, and it does not wait for run(). ShareSheetModel.swift:194-201 awaits queue.cancel() and then sets state = .closed. ShareSheetView.swift:32-33 then calls onCancel(). The init answer and the deleteUpload at the next cancelling check (e.g. :435-437) run later, so the extension can complete first and the opened session may not be deleted. This is a timing risk that I did not reproduce at runtime.

specification_compliance: I4 is violated by F1: the picked drive is not applied to the queue, and the saved items are resent.
I6/I7 are at risk from F2 and F3: a retry of an unknown item takes the .first path, and an unreachable error at /complete skips the polling.
I6 (cancel before /complete leaves no file) is at risk from F4.
regression_risks: Fixing F1 means routing DrivePicker to the queue when the state is stopped(.driveNotAvailable) and then calling queue.retry. That interacts with F2, because retry uses .first for every item.
test_coverage: I did not inspect the tests. The pickDriveForQueue path has no caller, so no UI-level test exercises it.
not_verified: Runtime behaviour of the extension when cancelled mid-init.
The backend, the frontend and the other invariants (I1, I2, I5, I8-I10).
